title: Opinions with reasons
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: present congiuntivo — four cells only (sia, abbia, possa, vada)
allowedPatterns: Penso che / Credo che / Mi sembra che + <congiuntivo>

rules.text: THE CONGIUNTIVO OPENS HERE, ON ONE TRIGGER AND FOUR CELLS. penso che, credo che and mi sembra che do not take the verb form you already know: after them è becomes sia, ha becomes abbia, può becomes possa and va becomes vada. Those four are the whole of it in this module. The mood as a SYSTEM — every verb, every tense, every other trigger — is L4's and is not opened here. Four cells on one trigger is what buys a learner the sentences they actually say.

ENGLISH MAPS STRAIGHT ONTO THE WRONG THING. "I think that it is true" runs word for word into penso che è vero, and that sentence is wrong. The English verb does not change after "I think", so nothing warns you that the Italian one must. An Italian hears the indicative there at once — it is not a small slip that passes — which is the whole reason the mood cannot wait for L4. The one loud thing in this module: after penso che, credo che and mi sembra che, the verb moves.

THE ESCAPE HATCH IS WORTH AS MUCH AS THE RULE. When BOTH halves have the same subject, Italian does not use che at all: penso DI avere ragione, credo DI tornare presto. Penso che io abbia ragione is grammatical and nobody says it. L1-M9 shipped penso di with a plain verb after it and left the reason for later; the reason is this. Half of what a learner wants to say about their own opinion needs no mood at all.

ANCHE SE TAKES THE PLAIN INDICATIVE. anche se costa molto, anche se è vero — never anche se costi. It is the counterweight to rule 0 and it sits in the same module on purpose: the mood belongs to the TRIGGER and not to the idea of a subordinate clause. A learner who has just met penso che sia will reach for the mood everywhere, and this is the first place that goes wrong.

TWO OPINION PHRASES THAT ARE NOT VERBS. secondo me needs no verb at all and is the cheapest useful thing in the module — two words and then your claim. sono d'accordo is an ADJECTIVE phrase carried by essere, never a verb of its own: never accordo, never mi accordo. Its apostrophe is inside one key with a straight mark, per the elision law, and it answers for nothing else.

SOFTENING IS A FRAME AT THE FRONT, NOT A WEAKENING OF THE CLAIM. Italian states an opinion plainly and marks it as an opinion before it starts: secondo me, forse, magari, non sono sicuro. Hedging the claim itself — trailing away, half-saying it — reads as evasive rather than polite. Neither language is the courteous one; they put the courtesy in different places, and Italian puts it in the first two words.

sentences.display: Secondo me questo ristorante è molto buono
sentences.cue: In my opinion this restaurant is very good
sentences.literal: Second me this restaurant is very good

words.note: ONE key of two words, so the bare me is not spent. It needs no verb: two words and then the claim. English's "according to me" sounds arrogant; this does not.

sentences.trap: The pronoun is me and not mi. mi is the little word that leans on a verb — mi piace, mi alzo — and me is what stands after a preposition, exactly as in L2-M5's per me. secondo takes the second kind.
sentences.sound: se-KON-do me. Both words are stressed on the syllable before last, and the me is a full clear e, not a schwa.

sentences.usage: The first two words of most spoken opinions, and they cost no verb at all.

sentences.display: Penso che questo libro sia molto bello
sentences.cue: I think this book is very good
sentences.literal: I-think that this book be very beautiful

words.note: The opinion verb standing on its own, without L1-M9's di. penso che opens a clause with its OWN subject, and that clause takes the congiuntivo.
The congiuntivo of è, and the only shape allowed after penso che. Two syllables, SEE-a. One shape covers io, tu and lui: penso che sia vero.

sentences.trap: English says "I think that this book is" and the verb never moves, so nothing in the English sentence warns you. Penso che questo libro è is the single most common thing an English speaker gets wrong in Italian, and it is heard immediately.
sentences.sound: PEN-so ke SEE-a. sia is two syllables and never rhymes with the English "see"; the a is fully sounded.

variations.display: Penso che questo libro sia molto utile
variations.cue: I think this book is very useful
variations.changed: the judgement

variations.display: Credo che questo vino sia buono
variations.cue: I think this wine is good
variations.changed: the other trigger, same mood

variations.display: Non penso che sia caro
variations.cue: I don't think it's expensive
variations.changed: negated, with the subject left out

mistake.display: Penso che questo libro è molto bello
mistake.why: penso che takes the congiuntivo: Penso che questo libro sia molto bello.

sentences.usage: Any opinion about a thing rather than about yourself, which is most of them.

sentences.display: Credo che mia sorella abbia ragione
sentences.cue: I think my sister is right
sentences.literal: I-believe that my sister have reason

words.note: The same job as penso and a shade more considered, not more religious. It takes the same clause and the same mood: credo che sia, credo che abbia.
The congiuntivo of ho, hai and ha — one shape for all three persons. credo che abbia ragione, never credo che ha ragione.
Italian HAS reason where English IS right: ho ragione, hai ragione, never sono ragione. A feminine noun, and it takes no article in the phrase.

sentences.trap: abbia hides the person. io abbia, tu abbia and lei abbia are one shape, so where English's verb tells you who, the Italian congiuntivo does not — which is why the subject is named out loud whenever it is not obvious from the room.
sentences.sound: KRE-do ke AB-bya ra-JO-ne. The double b is held, and the gi of ragione is a soft j.

variations.display: Credo che mio fratello abbia ragione
variations.cue: I think my brother is right
variations.changed: who is right

variations.display: Penso che tu abbia ragione
variations.cue: I think you're right
variations.changed: the tu subject, and the same abbia

variations.display: Non credo che abbia ragione
variations.cue: I don't think he's right
variations.changed: negated, with no subject named

mistake.display: Credo che mia sorella ha ragione
mistake.why: credo che takes the congiuntivo: Credo che mia sorella abbia ragione.

sentences.usage: Conceding a point about somebody who is not in the room.
sentences.mnemonic: One abbia for io, tu and lei.

sentences.display: Mi sembra che mio fratello possa aiutare
sentences.cue: It seems to me my brother can help
sentences.literal: To-me it-seems that my brother can to-help

words.note: ONE key with the pronoun and the che inside it, so the bare mi stays L2-M5's. The softest of the three triggers, and it takes the same mood as the other two.
The congiuntivo of posso, puoi and può — one shape for all three. What follows it is still a bare infinitive: possa aiutare, never possa di aiutare.

sentences.trap: The mood changes the modal and not what comes after it. L3-M2's law still holds — devo lavorare, posso studiare, possa aiutare — and nothing goes between the two verbs whichever shape the first one is in.
sentences.sound: mee SEM-bra ke POS-sa. The double s of possa is held, and sembra keeps its m and b as one blur.

variations.display: Mi sembra che mia sorella possa aiutare
variations.cue: It seems to me my sister can help
variations.changed: who can help

variations.display: Mi sembra che il capo possa tornare presto
variations.cue: It seems to me the boss can come back early
variations.changed: a different infinitive after possa

variations.display: Mi sembra caro
variations.cue: It seems expensive to me
variations.changed: no clause at all, so no che and no mood

mistake.display: Mi sembra che mio fratello può aiutare
mistake.why: mi sembra che takes the congiuntivo: Mi sembra che mio fratello possa aiutare.

sentences.usage: Putting an opinion on the table without owning it, which is what this frame is for.

sentences.display: Non credo che vada bene così
sentences.cue: I don't think it works like that
sentences.literal: Not I-believe that go well so

words.note: The congiuntivo of vado, vai and va — and the same shape L2-M4 taught as the polite go. The polite imperative IS this mood, which is why one form does both jobs.

sentences.trap: va bene is "it works", not "it goes well", so non credo che vada bene is the ordinary Italian no. Said with the mood in place it is a considered refusal; said as non credo che va bene it is the same refusal with a mistake in it.
sentences.sound: non KRE-do ke VA-da BE-ne ko-ZEE. così carries its stress on the final ì and the s is a soft z.

variations.display: Non credo che vada bene
variations.cue: I don't think it works
variations.changed: shorter, with no così

variations.display: Penso che vada bene così
variations.cue: I think it works like that
variations.changed: the positive, and the other trigger

variations.display: Non credo che vada a casa
variations.cue: I don't think he's going home
variations.changed: vada doing its literal go job

mistake.display: Non credo che va bene così
mistake.why: The trigger is still there under the non: Non credo che vada bene così.

sentences.usage: The polite Italian no to a plan, and the sentence a meeting turns on.
sentences.mnemonic: vada — the polite go, and the mood's go.

sentences.display: Penso di avere ragione, ma forse no
sentences.cue: I think I'm right, but maybe not
sentences.literal: I-think of to-have reason, but perhaps no

words.note: The infinitive of ho, hai and ha, and what follows penso di. It is the verb inside avere ragione, where Italian has the reason English is.
Sits where English's "maybe" sits — in front of the clause or at the end — and changes nothing around it. It never triggers the congiuntivo.

sentences.trap: This is the escape hatch. Both halves here are about ME, so Italian drops the che entirely and uses di plus a plain infinitive. Penso che io abbia ragione is grammatical and nobody says it — the mood is for when the second subject is somebody else.
sentences.sound: PEN-so dee a-VE-re ra-JO-ne. avere is stressed on the middle syllable, a-VE-re.

variations.display: Penso di avere ragione
variations.cue: I think I'm right
variations.changed: without the hedge

variations.display: Credo di avere ragione
variations.cue: I believe I'm right
variations.changed: the other trigger, still with di

variations.display: Penso di tornare a casa
variations.cue: I think I'll go back home
variations.changed: a different infinitive after di

mistake.why: Same subject in both halves takes di and an infinitive: Penso di avere ragione.

sentences.usage: Standing your ground and leaving the door open in the same breath.
sentences.mnemonic: Same subject → penso di. No mood at all.

sentences.display: Sono d'accordo, anche se costa molto
sentences.cue: I agree, even if it's expensive
sentences.literal: I-am in-agreement, even if it-costs a-lot

words.note: An adjective phrase carried by essere, never a verb of its own: never accordo, never mi accordo. The straight apostrophe is inside one key, answering for nothing else.
Takes the plain indicative: anche se costa, never anche se costi. English's "even if" gives no warning either way, so the habit has to be built here.

sentences.trap: Not every clause after an opinion bends. penso che takes the mood because of penso che; anche se does not, and the two sit in one module precisely so they never blur into "anything after an opinion goes congiuntivo".
sentences.sound: so-no dak-KOR-do. The d and the a run into one syllable, and the double c is held.

variations.display: Non sono d'accordo, anche se è vero
variations.cue: I don't agree, even if it's true
variations.changed: the negative, with the same indicative after anche se

variations.display: Sono d'accordo con il capo
variations.cue: I agree with the boss
variations.changed: who you agree with, and no second clause

variations.display: Sono d'accordo, anche se non è caro
variations.cue: I agree, even if it isn't expensive
variations.changed: the reason negated

mistake.why: d'accordo is an adjective and needs essere: Sono d'accordo, anche se costa molto.

sentences.usage: Agreeing while naming the cost of agreeing, which is how most agreements are said.
sentences.mnemonic: penso che bends. anche se does not.

sentences.display: Non sono d'accordo, perché non è vero
sentences.cue: I don't agree, because it isn't true
sentences.literal: Not I-am in-agreement, because not it-is true

words.note: An ordinary four-shape adjective. È vero is a whole sentence for "that's true", with nothing standing in front of the verb.

sentences.trap: The reason hangs off perché and nothing else moves: perché takes the plain indicative, exactly as anche se does. Only the three opinion triggers bend the verb, and perché is not one of them.
sentences.sound: non SO-no dak-KOR-do per-KE non e VE-ro. perché carries its stress on the final é.

variations.display: Non è vero
variations.cue: That's not true
variations.changed: the bare denial, with no frame

variations.display: Non sono d'accordo, perché è caro
variations.cue: I don't agree, because it's expensive
variations.changed: a different reason

variations.display: Penso che sia vero
variations.cue: I think it's true
variations.changed: the same adjective under a trigger, so the verb moves

mistake.display: Non sono d'accordo, perché non vero
mistake.why: The verb is not optional: Non sono d'accordo, perché non è vero.

sentences.usage: Disagreeing with the reason attached, which is the only shape that lands well.
sentences.mnemonic: Disagree, then say why — and perché does not bend.

sentences.display: Magari hai ragione, ma non sono d'accordo
sentences.cue: Maybe you're right, but I don't agree
sentences.literal: Maybe you-have reason, but not I-am in-agreement

words.note: Two lives. In front of a plain verb it is "maybe", warmer than forse. On its own, Magari! is "if only!" — English has no single word that does both.

sentences.trap: magari in front of a plain verb is only "maybe" and takes no che. Alone it is a wish, and the two are told apart by what follows rather than by the word, so a learner who meets the wish first will hear the maybe as enthusiasm.
sentences.sound: ma-GA-ree. The stress is on the middle syllable, and the g is hard.

variations.display: Magari hai ragione
variations.cue: Maybe you're right
variations.changed: the concession on its own

variations.display: Forse hai ragione, ma non è vero
variations.cue: Maybe you're right, but it isn't true
variations.changed: the cooler softener in its place

variations.display: Magari torniamo domani
variations.cue: Maybe we'll come back tomorrow
variations.changed: a plain verb after it, and no opinion at all

mistake.display: Magari che hai ragione, ma non sono d'accordo
mistake.why: magari takes no che in front of a plain verb: Magari hai ragione.

sentences.usage: Giving someone the point and keeping your position, in one sentence.
sentences.mnemonic: Magari! is a wish. Magari hai ragione is a maybe.

sentences.display: Non sono sicuro, quindi penso di tornare
sentences.cue: I'm not sure, so I think I'll go back
sentences.literal: Not I-am sure, therefore I-think of to-return

words.note: A four-shape adjective, so a woman says non sono sicura. It hedges the frame around a claim and leaves the claim itself standing.

sentences.trap: Non sono sicuro softens the FRAME, and the claim after it stays plain. Trailing off in the middle of the claim itself is not politeness in Italian — it reads as evasion, and the hedge belongs in front where a listener can hear it coming.
sentences.sound: see-KOO-ro. quindi is KWEEN-dee, with the qu as a full kw.

variations.display: Non sono sicura, quindi penso di tornare
variations.cue: I'm not sure, so I think I'll go back
variations.changed: a woman speaking, so the adjective moves

variations.display: Non sono sicuro, ma penso di andare
variations.cue: I'm not sure, but I think I'll go
variations.changed: ma instead of quindi, and a different infinitive

variations.display: Secondo me è meglio tornare
variations.cue: In my opinion it's better to go back
variations.changed: the frame from S01, with no hedge at all

mistake.display: Non sono sicuro, quindi penso tornare
mistake.why: penso needs its di before an infinitive: quindi penso di tornare.

sentences.usage: Getting out of a decision honestly, with the reason and the plan in one line.
sentences.mnemonic: Hedge the frame. Never the claim.
